summary: Introductory security intake focused on payment-regulated constraints. Fjordline emphasized PCI concerns, short retention windows for logs and model inputs, and a hard requirement for BYOK/HSM-backed KMS in the EU. Redwood AE/SE walked through hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs; SE flagged audit-log retention controls, RBAC scoping, SAML flows, and canary fallback behaviors. Customer asked for SOC2 evidence, ISO scope, SSO config examples, and an architecture diagram for Private. Call closed with explicit next steps to share artifacts and set pilot kickoff.
topics: SSO / SAML integration and IdP specifics
RBAC and least privilege for inference endpoints
Audit logs, retention windows, and exportability
Encryption / KMS BYOK, HSM, and key rotation
Data residency and purge policies for model inputs
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for PCI use-cases
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-03-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Oliver (Fjordline Head of Security), Maya (VP Eng), Samir (Compliance), Noah (SRE)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for making time, i'll do a 1 minute intro, im lena with Redwood, we're the inference platform, focused on hosted, dedicated and private deployment options for teams running models in prod. Marcus and priya are here to handle technical/security and ops.

[00:18] Oliver Nyberg: great thanks lena, yeah we run payments services so main themes today are PCI, data retention, and key management. we want to understand where customer's data lives, length of retention for logs and model prompts, and whether we can bring our own keys to satisfy our certs.

[00:35] Marcus Chen: sure, quick outline — we'll walk through high-level deployment options, then deep-dive on audit logs, sso/saml flows, and KMS / BYOK. we'll also note known limitations, latency/cost tradeoffs. excuse my notes are a bit messy — i typed while on mobile.

[01:02] Maya Singh: just to flag — our compliance team requires either private (vpc) or dedicated with an encrypted tenant; hosted is tough unless you can guarantee BYOK and EU-only residency and retention policies.

[01:18] Lena Ortiz: totally understood. for context, most payment-y customers end up evaluating dedicated first, sometimes moving to private when they need full network control or air-gap. we have customers on Hosted who are SOC2'd but typically with additional contractual controls.

[01:43] Samir Patel: can you speak to SOC 2? is that Type II? and do you have ISO 27001? we need evidence for our auditors.

[01:55] Lena Ortiz: yes we have SOC2 Type II — i'll share the report, plus our ISO 27001 cert scope. we'll follow up with the redacted artifacts.

[02:10] Marcus Chen: on SSO — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC; we've got SAML flows in both Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SAML for console / admin, and you can federate via SSO for token provisioning. small note: the session timeouts default on hosted are configurable via enterprise plan.

[02:42] Noah Eriksen: how does auth map to RBAC? we have separate teams — product, ops, fraud — need least-privilege.

[02:51] Marcus Chen: our RBAC model uses role-based policies per route and per model. you can scope roles to view-only / invoke / manage models / access logs. for Private we expose more granular IAM integrations e.g., map to your idp groups; for hosted we have a managed RBAC layer with auditability. we'll send a matrix with default roles and recommended minimums.

[03:22] Oliver Nyberg: audit logs — what events do you capture? we need per-request logs including request id, timestamp, user identity, model version, and query hash ideally. retention has to be configurable and exportable.

[03:36] Marcus Chen: we capture request metadata (request id, timestamp, model, route, tokens consumed), user principal, and service-level metrics. note: the transcript/text of the prompt is considered application data — retention is configurable but on hosted our standard tenant retention is 90 days by default; enterprise customers can request shorter or longer via contract and dedicated/private allow full control including retention TTL and deletions. export: logs can be streamed to your SIEM via S3/Kafka or syslog for Private/Dedicated; Hosted supports log export for enterprise tiers.

[04:10] Maya Singh: 90 days won't fly for payments — our lawyers want 7 days for prompt text retention and 180 days aggregate metrics. also we can't store PAN or raw card data in prompts; we tokenize before sending but need to know the platform won't persist raw payloads longer than TTL.

[04:30] Lena Ortiz: understood — Private gives you the ability to set TTL to 0 for model inputs or have an automated purge pipeline. for Dedicated we can negotiate shorter retention windows and contractual SLAs. we'll note Blackbox storage — by default we don't store raw tokens beyond TTL if configured.

[04:56] Samir Patel: KMS — do you support BYOK? HSM? key rotation? where are keys stored for hosted?

[05:08] Marcus Chen: Hosted supports a managed KMS but also supports Bring-Your-Own-Key via customer KMS integrations for enterprise customers; the model: you can either upload keys into Redwood's managed KMS or proxy encryption calls to your KMS (we support major cloud KMSes — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault). for Private you keep keys in your VPC and Redwood components reference them over the private network. HSM-backed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted BYOK typically uses cloud KMS-backed HSMs. rotation: we support key rotation policies and key versioning; re-encryption of stored objects is supported but we need to coordinate maintenance windows.

[05:50] Oliver Nyberg: proof — we need assurance that Redwood does not have plaintext access to our keys or data when BYOK is enabled. is there a zero-key-access mode?

[06:03] Marcus Chen: for BYOK we can configure envelope encryption where the root key never leaves your KMS and Redwood only gets ephemeral data keys. in that mode, Redwood cannot decrypt without your KMS approving the unwrap. we'll document the flow and provide diagrams.

[06:25] Lena Ortiz: i'll include a flow diagram; note that some hosted features like live model caching may require ephemeral keys to be available to runtime — we can architect to minimize exposure.

[06:40] Maya Singh: what about audit logs for admin actions — who changed model versions, who rolled a rollout, can we push those logs to our SIEM?

[06:50] Marcus Chen: yes admin/audit trails are captured; for Dedicated/Private you can forward to your SIEM in near-real time. hosted enterprise supports log export to S3 or third-party destinations; retention policies can be applied server-side or by you once exported.

[07:15] Samir Patel: encryption at rest details? TLS? in transit? cert management?

[07:25] Marcus Chen: TLS 1.2+ mandatory in transit. at rest everything is encrypted using customer-managed keys when BYOK is enabled otherwise platform-managed keys. certificate rotation uses standard ACME workflows for public endpoints; for Private you manage certs. we can provide certificate thumbprint verification steps.

[07:48] Oliver Nyberg: data residency — we need EU-only processing for EU customers. can Redwood guarantee EU-only compute for Hosted?

[07:58] Lena Ortiz: yes we have regional hosting and can pin your tenant to an EU region; for absolute guarantee with strict network egress constraints customers choose Private in their own VPC or Dedicated capacity in the EU. we'll provide region pinning docs.

[08:16] Noah Eriksen: fallback behavior — if Dedicated capacity is down or throttled what happens? do you fall back to hosted and if so, how do we ensure compliance?

[08:29] Marcus Chen: we have smart routing policies — you can configure failover rules. default is to fail open to a lower-tier model in same region; you can disable cross-environment fallback to avoid moving data outside of your bound. for PCI we generally recommend disabling auto-fallback to hosted unless explicitly allowed.

[08:55] Maya Singh: do you have data deletion / purge APIs? and proof of deletion?

[09:04] Marcus Chen: yes we expose deletion APIs; for Private you have direct control. for Hosted we perform deletions and can provide deletion receipts and an audit trail. for higher assurance we can schedule secure overwrite windows and produce attestation.

[09:25] Lena Ortiz: quick question for samir — are you planning to run any PII in prompts or will all cardholder data be tokenized before hitting Redwood?

[09:34] Samir Patel: everything must be tokenized first; we may include last4 occasionally. compliance wants an explicit statement that the platform won't reconstruct PAN from tokenized prompts.

[09:45] Marcus Chen: we don't do any token rehydration unless you request a data service that we run under contract. typical flow: tokenization is managed by customer pre-ingest. we'll add a sentence to the security pack confirming we do not attempt to reconstruct tokens.

[10:01] Maya Singh: what about model caching and KV cache — does that persist prompts? how do you ensure that KV cache doesn't leak?

[10:12] Marcus Chen: good point. KV cache is an optimization for generation; we can configure it to drop sensitive context or not cache at all for tenant routes. for Private you can disable cross-request caching, and for Dedicated we can apply tenant-specific cache policies. this will be in the RBAC / runtime config doc.

[10:36] Oliver Nyberg: regulatory — auditors will want to see processes for key compromise, incident response, and breach notification SLAs. can we get those docs?

[10:45] Priya Rao: yes, incident response runbook, breach notification timelines, and playbooks are part of our enterprise pack. i'll attach those. typical timeline is 72 hours for notification plus patch/action items, but we can discuss SLA specifics.

[11:02] Samir Patel: retention of audit logs — we may need immutable logs for 180 days for legal hold. is immutability supported?

[11:10] Marcus Chen: we support write-once S3 exports and can integrate with your WORM storage or third-party immutability. for Private you can implement immutability in your storage stack; for hosted we'll broker with enterprise S3 policies and object lock.

[11:32] Maya Singh: OK regarding timelines — we want SOC2 artifacts by next week, then the architecture diagram and SAML example, then pilot kickoff. approximate cost question — dedicated vs private rough delta?

[11:44] Lena Ortiz: high level: Dedicated is lower operational burden, predictable monthly commit for GPU capacity. Private has higher upfront ops but maximum control; pricing delta depends on committed GPUs and support level, i'll include a sample cost sheet.

[11:58] Oliver Nyberg: any customers in payments space we can talk to as references?

[12:05] Lena Ortiz: we can provide references under NDA; i'll include a short roster.

[12:12] Samir Patel: final: we need to confirm whether Redwood performs any human-in-the-loop review of prompts or data for product ops.

[12:23] Marcus Chen: no human review of customer prompts for hosted telemetry. we may surface anonymized traces for system debugging but never with customer identifiable data unless you opt-in for support sessions. we'll capture that in the privacy doc.

[12:40] Lena Ortiz: great — to recap next steps: i'll send SOC2/ISO pack and references; marcus will send architecture diagrams, RBAC matrix and SAML sample; priya will schedule pilot kickoff calendar; oliver will share retention and tokenization requirements. any blockers?

[12:59] Oliver Nyberg: sounds good, main blocker is internal legal signoff but these artifacts will help. thanks.

[13:12] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and slack. end call.

Notes on quality: transcription missed a few proper nouns (some infra names were garbled), occasional overlapping speech at 10:12-10:36.
